title: All-hands lightning Q&A sprint notes (scratch)
content:
Goal: draft a lightweight operational script for the 'lightning Q&A sprint' segment in the March all-hands. Keep it short (10–12 mins), high signal, low broadcast. This doc = scratch notes for rehearsal + moderator cues.

Format I want to pilot (timebox 12m total):
- 60s framing from CEO (context + ask: keep Qs short, tag follow-ups)
- 60s moderator rules (how we pick, when we escalate)
- 8m rapid-fire live Q&A (6–8 questions, ~60–80s each incl. follow-up)
- 2–3m lightning wrap + next steps (links, owners, follow-up cadence)

Moderator role (primary: Maya; backup: Noor):
- Watch live queue in Slack + Zoom reactions. Pick short, high-impact Qs first (product, reliability, roadmap signals).
- Triage: if question needs a long technical dive, acknowledge and promise a deeper doc/office hour with owner within 48h.
- Signal using three quick labels in Slack thread: FLASH (answer now), DEEP (defer to follow-up), SENSITIVE (requires comms/legal review).
- Keep time: gentle 60–80s nudge if answer is going long. Use the chat to post follow-up tasks immediately.

Pre-selection heuristics (how we choose the 6–8 to surface live):
- Prefer questions that: 1) affect a lot of users/teams, 2) are clarifying vs speculative, 3) can be answered succinctly.
- Reserve 1 slot for product roadmap ask, 1 for infra/reliability, 1 for pricing/billing ops, 1 float for surprise topical.
- If we get >40 Qs, pick highest-upvoted and then sample by org to avoid bias.

Suggested moderator script (bullet points, very short):
- "Thanks — quick rules: short Q, quick answer. If we need a deep dive we’ll capture it and schedule a follow-up. Tagging owners live."
- For each Q: "Q from @handle: [one-line summary]. [Answer — 40–60s]. Follow-up: [who, when]."

Examples of tricky questions + draft short replies (practice phrasing):
1) Q: "Are we pausing new model onboarding because of the recent latency regressions?"
   Draft reply: "No blanket pause. We slowed a few experimental rollouts and enabled a canary gate for new models. We have an internal pause checklist and will share a short postmortem in 48h. Owner: SRE (Ravi)."

2) Q: "Will pricing change after the Dedicated launch?"
   Draft reply: "Core hosted pricing stays stable. Dedicated is contract-based and may have different tiers. We’ll publish formal docs next week. Owner: Product & Pricing (Maya)."

3) Q: "How does Private deployment roadmap align with APAC expansion?"
   Draft reply: "Private is independent but we’re prioritizing APAC-region readiness for both hosted and private. Timeline: phased—region infra by Q2, private packaging improvements by Q3. Owner: Infra PM (Noor)."

Escalation language for SENSITIVE / Legal questions (templates):
- "We hear the concern. That looks like it needs legal/compliance input. We’ll capture, escalate, and come back with a summary in the follow-up doc. Owner: Legal & Security review (TBD)."

On follow-ups and ownership capture (live ops):
- Immediately after answering, moderator posts a one-line task in #all-hands-followups: title, short summary, owner, ETA (48–72h).
- Follow-up tracker: simple sheet row => question, answer summary, owner, ETA, status. Post link in chat and add to the all-hands Confluence page.

Rehearsal checklist (before CEO time):
- Moderator + CEO run 1x full dry run (7–10m) with canned Qs.
- Confirm Slack thread is unlocked and reactions are enabled.
- Confirm backup presenter (Noor) can take over if connection drops.
- Put follow-up sheet link in the Zoom chat.

Potential pitfalls + mitigation (notes to self):
- Pitfall: Someone asks roadmap for unreleased big feature -> Mitigation: high-level statement + commitment to product blog/roadmap doc, no specifics.
- Pitfall: Live outage question escalates emotionally -> Mitigation: defer to SRE postmortem, give calm statement and next-steps.
- Pitfall: Pricing/legal minutiae asked live -> Mitigation: acknowledge, escalate to Legal, promise a precise written answer.

Post-mortem / measurement (what signals to track):
- Slack thread reaction count / upvotes on surfaced Qs.
- % of surfaced Qs that turned into tracked follow-ups (aim < 30% deferred to deep).
- Survey 1–2 question pulse after all-hands: "Was the Q&A useful?" + free text.
- Time adherence (target: <=12m).

Open TODOs (my action items):
- [ ] Draft one-pager for moderators with labels and quick Slack macros (due 2026-03-11).
- [ ] Create follow-up sheet and add template row (done? need to create).
- [ ] Send rehearsal invite to CEO + Maya + Noor + Ravi (outreach in progress).
- [ ] Prepare 8 canned practice Qs and answers (I’ll draft tonight).

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep language simple and avoid 'technical-speak' during live segment. Laypeople in audience.
- If CEO overruns, switch to 6m Q&A and hold rest for AMA Slack thread.

Scratch: potential canned Qs (framing):
- "What happened with last week's latency blip?"
- "Any changes to token billing next quarter?"
- "Is there an ETA on the private deployment package for on-prem?"
- "How are we addressing support capacity for Dedicated customers?"
- "What’s the plan for handling more model variants in the catalog?"

Keep this doc as canonical rehearsal scratch. After rehearsal I’ll move finalized script to Confluence and create follow-up tracker link.

References / quick links I want to paste into final:
- Confluence event page (linked above)
- Follow-up sheet (create after rehearsal)
- Slack channel: #all-hands, #all-hands-followups

Random thought: if lightning format lands, make it a recurring pattern and publish "how it works" page for new moderators.

-- Omri (scratch)
summary: Scratchpad for running a 12-minute "lightning Q&A sprint" during all-hands: moderator cues, triage rules, sample answers, rehearsal checklist, and follow-up process.
